tour.name: Qatar Desert Safari to the Inland Sea: Dune Bashing, Camel Ride & Sandboarding
tour.subtitle: A private 4x4 across the dunes south of Doha to Khor Al Adaid, where the sand meets a tidal sea, with a camel ride, sandboarding and time to swim or simply watch the light change.

tour.overview:
Qatar's most spectacular landscape lies an hour south of Doha. Beyond the industrial port of Mesaieed, the road ends at the Sealine dunes, and from there only four-wheel drives with deflated tyres can continue. Ahead lies Khor Al Adaid, the 'Inland Sea': a tidal inlet that reaches deep into the desert, with sand dunes sliding straight into turquoise water and, on the far shore, Saudi Arabia. It is one of the very few places in the world where the sea comes so far into a sand desert, and it is protected as a natural reserve.

This private safari takes you there with an experienced desert driver. After a stop at the camel station near Sealine for a short ride, the driver lets air out of the tyres and the dune bashing begins: a roller-coaster crossing of high, soft dunes, at a pace you choose. At the Inland Sea you have time to climb a dune for the view, swim or paddle from the beach, and try sandboarding down a slope. On the sunset departure, you watch the sun go down over the dunes before driving back to Doha in the dark.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 5 hours (morning or afternoon/sunset)
• Start and finish: your hotel in Doha
• Type: private 4x4 with an English-speaking desert driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Activity level: easy, but the dune bashing is bumpy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Sealine dunes and the camel station.
• Khor Al Adaid, the Inland Sea, with Saudi Arabia on the far shore.
• Sunset over the dunes (afternoon departure).

WHY THIS TOUR WORKS
You cannot drive to the Inland Sea in a normal car, and crossing the dunes needs both the right vehicle and a driver who reads the sand. A private safari means no waiting for a group: the driver adjusts the speed to your taste – thrilling or gentle – and you stay as long as you like at the water.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Couples, families with children over about five, friends looking for adventure, photographers and anyone on a Doha stopover who wants to see the desert.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
Dune bashing is not recommended during pregnancy or for people with back or heart problems: our Doha city tour or West Qatar tour are gentler alternatives.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Wear light clothes, a hat and sunglasses, and bring swimwear and a towel if you want to swim. From May to September choose the afternoon/sunset departure. Our cars carry water and soft drinks; take motion-sickness tablets before the dunes if you need them.

days.name: Desert Safari to the Inland Sea
days.description:
What to expect: a private 4x4 crossing of the dunes south of Doha to Khor Al Adaid, the Inland Sea, with a camel ride, sandboarding and time at the water.

Your driver collects you from your hotel in a 4x4 and heads south along the coast road, past the port town of Mesaieed, to the Sealine dunes, about an hour from Doha. At the camel station you meet the camels and take a short ride, and your driver lets air out of the tyres – soft tyres float over the sand instead of digging in.

Then the dune bashing begins: the car climbs, tips and slides across tall, soft dunes, sometimes along a ridge with the desert falling away on both sides. Your driver adapts the pace to the group; just say if you want more thrills or a gentler ride. After about forty minutes the dunes open onto Khor Al Adaid, the Inland Sea – a tidal inlet reaching deep into the desert, with sand slopes running straight into pale blue water and, across the channel, the coast of Saudi Arabia.

At the Inland Sea you have about an hour: climb a dune for the panorama, try sandboarding down a slope, swim or paddle from the beach, or just sit and watch the colours change. On the afternoon departure you stay for sunset over the dunes before the drive back, when the driver re-inflates the tyres at Sealine and returns you to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates; sunset departure in brackets)
07:30 (14:00) – Pick-up at your hotel in Doha.
08:30 (15:00) – Sealine: camel station and short camel ride.
09:00 (15:30) – Dune bashing towards the Inland Sea (about 40 minutes).
09:45 (16:15) – Khor Al Adaid: sandboarding, swimming, photos (about 1 hour).
10:45 (17:15) – Dune drive back to Sealine (sunset on the way in the afternoon).
12:30 (19:00) – Return to your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The dune drive is bumpy: not recommended during pregnancy or with back, neck or heart problems.
• Bring swimwear and a towel if you want to swim; there are no changing rooms at the Inland Sea.
• Quad biking at Sealine can be added on request, paid locally.
• An overnight in a desert camp at the Inland Sea can be arranged on request.

INCLUDED: private 4x4 and driver, dune bashing, camel ride, sandboarding, water and soft drinks, hotel pick-up.
NOT INCLUDED: quad biking, meals, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: none.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose your date, morning or sunset, and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only once your safari is confirmed.

faq.question: Morning or sunset safari?
faq.answer: The morning is cooler and the light is soft on the water. The afternoon departure ends with sunset over the dunes, which most travellers prefer from October to April. In summer, both are best started as early or as late as possible.

faq.question: Is dune bashing dangerous?
faq.answer: Our drivers are experienced desert drivers and the 4x4s are equipped for the dunes. It is a bumpy ride, so it is not recommended during pregnancy or for people with back, neck or heart problems. You can always ask the driver to slow down.

faq.question: Can children join?
faq.answer: Yes, from about five years old, with a child seat. Younger children can join if you ask the driver to keep the dune crossing gentle.

faq.question: How long is the camel ride?
faq.answer: About 10 to 15 minutes at the Sealine camel station – long enough for photos and the feeling of riding. Longer rides can be arranged on request.

faq.question: Can I swim at the Inland Sea?
faq.answer: Yes, the water is calm and warm for most of the year. There are no facilities or changing rooms, so wear your swimwear under your clothes and bring a towel.

faq.question: Is it really Saudi Arabia across the water?
faq.answer: Yes. Khor Al Adaid lies on the border, and the hills on the far shore of the channel are in Saudi Arabia. You cannot cross, but the view is part of the experience.

faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer: Light, loose clothes, a hat, sunglasses and sandals or trainers you don't mind filling with sand. In winter, take a light jacket for the sunset.

faq.question: Is food included?
faq.answer: Water and soft drinks are included. Meals are not, but a barbecue dinner at a desert camp can be added on request.

faq.question: Can we add quad biking?
faq.answer: Yes. Quad bikes can be rented at Sealine and paid locally; tell us when booking so we plan the time.

faq.question: Can we stay overnight in the desert?
faq.answer: Yes. Desert camps at the Inland Sea offer dinner and a night in a tent. We can arrange it on request as an extension of this safari.

faq.question: How many people fit in one car?
faq.answer: Up to five travellers per 4x4. Larger groups travel in convoy with several cars and drivers.

faq.question: What is your cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the safari. Before your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
